I retrieved and handed papers, opened boxes, checked the petri-dish delivery status on my phone/WeChat (scrolled, typed, then set phone down), watched Tasha’s demonstration, and repeatedly nodded. Conclusion: seed paper and petri-dish sprouting were accepted as eco-friendly activity options.

**Alice proposes wildlife puzzle and daffodil-bulb prizes** Alice proposed a challenging wildlife puzzle representing Earth harmony and suggested giving narcissus (daffodil) bulbs as participant prizes, offering to purchase quality bulbs. I observed, nodded, laughed, applauded, and acknowledged the prize idea. Conclusion: puzzle plus bulb prizes were added to the activity list.

**Katrina’s planting kits and Shure’s auction/cardboard idea** Katrina mentioned Haidilao’s strawberry planting kit and other planting options; group noted planting kits and short-term sprouting. Shure proposed a second-hand auction and reiterated cardboard availability. I reacted verbally (“Haidilao,” “Let’s go plant trees by the sea”), shifted positions, clapped, and rose as Shure began detailing his auction idea. Conclusion: the team accumulated four activities and progressed to Shure’s pitch.
